scope: Theorem 1.1 (Strip mass and bridge length) of the manuscript “Polynomial vacuum representations and bridge mass for honeycomb walks” (preprints/Polynomial-vacuum-representations-and-bridge-mass-for-honeycomb-walks-September-26-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 237 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 69885ae7308d1f03), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 2. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: As the integer layer height h tends to infinity, bh = h−1/4+o(1) , ℓh = h13/12+o(1) , Eh|γ| = h4/3+o(1) . All three sums are finite. These exponents are unchanged if the paths are also confined to horizontal distance h log2 h from their initial port.
